text:
ravi: Canary for release v2.14.3 blocked by deploy-bot — SBOM provenance mismatch on image gcr.io/redwood/v2.14.3-canary

deploy-bot: Canary quarantined: SBOM provenance mismatch + vuln-scan: 1 HIGH (CVE-2024-1450) in transitive dep `libfastjson`
```
reason: SBOM signer not found for layer sha256:4a3f...
vuln: CVE-2024-1450 - severity:HIGH - path: /app/.venv/libfastjson
```

maya: Ack. Change window closes in ~2h. What's our appetite for pin vs rollback? Any signed SBOM we can trust? :thinking_face:

jordan: We don't have a signed SBOM for that image, SBOM generator shows provenance missing signature for the base layer. Options:
- Pin transitive dep to docker digest that matches verified SBOM (fastest)
- Build new image with backported patch (longer, but cleaner)
- Rollback to v2.14.2 (safe, known-good)
Need approval audit trail for pinning if we go that route.

olga: QA: smoke/regression passed on v2.14.3 except for one fuzz test that touches JSON parsing (likely libfastjson). v2.14.2 passes all tests.

ravi: My preference is to try a targeted pin + re-run SBOM + vuln scan in staging. If that fixes it and we get a signed SBOM, we can resume canary within the window. If not, rollback. Keep global rollout blocked.

maya: Agree with staged pin attempt. Decision: Hold global rollout. Attempt pinned image build -> regenerate SBOM with signature -> re-run vuln-scan. Timebox 60 minutes. If green, @jordan to sign off, @devops-bot to promote to canary. If still failing, rollback to v2.14.2 and record in release notes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jordan: I'll approve the pin if SBOM is signed and CLA/license checks are green. Creating ticket SEC-4123 and adding reviewers. ETA ~45m to validate.

devops-bot: Starting build for pinned image (pin libfastjson@sha256:9b2c...). Running sbom-generator v1.4 -> will publish SBOM to s3://sboms/canaries/1718279142-pinned.json

deploy-bot: Will run vuln-scan after SBOM publish. If no HIGH/CRITICAL, will wait for explicit sign-off from jordan before unquarantine.

ravi: I'll draft the brief release note lines now to save time:
```
- Hold: v2.14.3 global rollout paused due to SBOM provenance mismatch and transient vuln in transitive dep.
- Action: pinned transitive dependency libfastjson to known digest; running verification and signature. If verification fails, will rollback to v2.14.2 and open follow-up.
```

maya: Nice. Please include changelog bullet referencing SEC-4123.

olga: Noted — QA will run the extended JSON fuzz suite against the pinned image once build finishes.

jordan: Update: I'm on the review, will comment on SEC-4123 with approve/reject within 45m. If approved, I will add an approval note that can be attached to the SBOM for audit.

ravi: Thanks everyone. Keeping thread here for final decision. If we end up rolling back, I'll put a short postmortem in #postmortems and update the release notes before the next change window. :thumbsup:
